notes.title: Gamescom 2025: Life Below Preview — Under the Sea!
notes.content:
I am often heard complaining that similar genres seem to surge in popularity all at once. It certainly happened with cozy farming simulators and is currently happening with extraction shooters. After accepting my Life Below appointment at gamescom 2025, I was bombarded with city builders, too. It seems that as soon as I am looking for something, it pops up consistently. With that said, I am always happy to see a studio do something different with an oversaturated genre, and developer Megapop is doing just that with Life Below.

I was able to sit down with Game Director Lise Hagen Lie and have her walk me through the game in a quick 30-minute demo that showed me various stages of the game from beginning to end, after players are more established. Though it doesn’t look like your typical city builder, Life Below is just that, only for marine life. You’re not just building typical housing and commercial buildings. notes.title: Life Below Makes Its Gamescom Debut!
notes.content: [p]Kasedo Games & Megapop are excited to bring Life Below to Gamescom 2025! We can’t wait for you to dive into our sub-aquatic reef builder at Hall 7.1, Booth A02. For the first time ever, the game is available in multiple languages: English, German, Japanese, French, Russian, Italian, Spanish, and Chinese (Simplified).[/p][p]Explore, expand, and protect your reef as Thalassa, facing dynamic underwater challenges while discovering new wildlife.[/p][p]Check out the gameplay trailer: [/p][previewyoutube="kPnwgfkst8s;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Swim over to [url="https://discord.gg/HjWS2xVWqE"]our Discord[/url] for all the latest updates and make waves on Steam by wishlisting Life Below today![/p]

notes.title: Life Below will be playable at Gamescom!
notes.content: [p]Life Below blends realism with fantasy in a unique twist on the city-builder genre and you can be among the first to help restore the ocean at Gamescom, in Cologne later this month.[/p][p]The ocean is on the brink. Coral reefs are vanishing, ecosystems are collapsing and the deep sea is struggling. As fledgling reef guardian Thalassa, you must restore balance, using the ocean floor itself as the foundation to build a new vibrant sea life.[/p][p]In this underwater city-builder with elements of resource management and survival, you won’t be placing buildings and roads - instead you’ll strategically grow coral, create bustling reefs and attract diverse marine species to use their abilities and bring colour back into the depths of the ocean.[/p][p]Experience Thalassa’s journey at Gamescom on 20-24th August. See you there![/p][p][/p]

notes.title: This underwater city builder had me more emotionally invested in my corals than SimCity does in my human citizens, and you can try it at the next Steam Next Fest
notes.content: I love metropolitan city builders, but once I'm done turning fertile riverside plains into a mess of eight-lane highways and coal plants, I can't help but wonder if I've maybe been a net negative for the world around me. When I saw Life Below on Steam—a city builder all about constructing reefs that opens its Steam description with "the ocean is dying"—I was flooded with the exact blend of guilt and intrigue I look for in my entertainment... Read more.

notes.title: Introducing Life Below…
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=py6eh7b-Umg;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re a fan of city builders, this one’s for you - but with an ocean twist… Kasedo Games are teaming up with Megapop, the talented studio behind Life Below, to bring an underwater city-builder to life.

In Life Below, you’re not building cities.. You’re building reefs. Think chill strategy meets underwater eco-restoration. Grow coral, attract sea creatures and evolve entire underwater ecosystems to survive the ever-changing ocean.

You play as Thalassa, a guardian of the deep, bringing life back into the oceans. You’ll grow and expand your reef, craft habitats, lure wildlife and tackle a range of ocean hazards.

We’re thrilled to have Rhianna Pratchett on board, bringing her incredible storytelling to this narrative-driven reef builder. Life Below also aims to be accessible to all, developed with accessibility consultant Arevya and the charity SpecialEffect, who are helping us shape features that make a real impact.

Life Below will be making a splash on Windows PC next year, but you won’t have to wait that long to test the waters! Try the demo on World Ocean Day (8 June) and during Steam Next Fest (9-16 June).
